_comment: Robotensor Vector's contract (Competition 1 of the subnet, action-grounded in-context learning): weights-only submissions of one architecture the validator owns the code of, scored in rolling king-of-the-hill duels on RoboTwin's level benchmark, cross-scene. Its own file beside spec.json, the code-submission contract, so neither changes the other; the subnet validator loads it with --spec. Bumping spec_version changes every derived duel id.

vector_level1.title: Vector: one demonstration from another scene, level 1
vector_level1.blurb: The policy is shown one demonstration of a task - the frames of three cameras, the action trajectory and the proprioception - recorded by RoboTwin's expert in one scene, and must do the task in another scene of the same level. Level 1 varies the objects' positions and yaw between the two. Submissions are weights of the BPP architecture only.
vector_level1._comment: Cross-scene: every unit's demonstration and evaluation scene are drawn from disjoint candidate lists, from seeds no public split of the level benchmark used, and the units are seeded from a chain block hash the challenger could not know when it committed. The difficulty rounds of the subnet spec are levels 1-4; this is level 1.

robotwin._comment: The RoboTwin fork with the level gate and the harness under bench/, branch vector. Installed editable from the fork, so pinned by version; a wheel pin follows the first release.

_benchmarks_comment: Every benchmark is a separate distribution found through the `robotensor.benchmarks` entry point group. The orchestrator ships none: what it can score is exactly what is plugged into it.

vector_level1.title: Sixteen tabletop tasks (two Franka arms, level 1)
vector_level1.blurb: RoboTwin's 16 pick-and-place and tool tasks of the level benchmark, dealt evenly over a duel's units. RoboTwin's expert produces the demonstration at evaluation time in one scene and its own check decides the outcome in another.

environment._comment: Each task carries its own step limit from RoboTwin (400-800). An ee action is [left x y z qw qx qy qz, left gripper, right x y z qw qx qy qz, right gripper].

_skills_comment: One skill, whose units the plugin deals evenly over the suite's 16 tasks; the published units carry each task, so per-task rates can be read off a record.

duel._crown_comment: Both sides run the identical unit list on identical prompt bytes. The challenger takes the crown iff challenger.average >= king.average + score_margin / 100 AND the one-sided exact sign test over the units exactly one side solved gives p <= alpha. Void units are excluded from both sides, and the duel is void when the void fraction exceeds max_void_fraction.
duel._sizes_comment: launch is 10 units per task and full is the subnet spec's 50. A unit is a demonstration expert run, an evaluation-scene expert check and two rollouts.

derivation.entropy: <seed_block>:<seed_block_hash>, the chain block the validator started the duel at (after the challenger's commitment) and its hash as the chain reports it
derivation.unit_id: <skills.<skill>.code>-<index over the track's units, three digits>

budgets._comment: Measured on one RTX PRO 6000: a level-1 materialize (demonstration plus evaluation-scene check) took 30-47 s and a 500-step rollout 38 s with a replay policy. A served BPP answers one act per executed step and predicts every 12. Generous for launch; tighten once duels are measured. stall_seconds: a benchmark process group using under 0.1 cores for that long is a hung SAPIEN render (a camera read that never returns), killed and started again up to stall_retries times with a fresh policy server; measured, a healthy rollout uses far more (a render every step is ~25 ms of a 0.14 s step).

submission._comment: A submission is a Hugging Face model repository at a resolved commit holding model.safetensors of the pinned BPP architecture and nothing else but a README. Its header is checked against the template before a tensor is read, and the validator's own code builds, loads and serves it: nothing of the submission ever runs, so no sandbox is needed.

media._comment: Clips are written by the benchmark's commands (demonstration.mp4 and evaluation.mp4) and stored content-addressed by sha256; the orchestrator does not encode video.

store._layout_comment: manifest.json; tracks/{track}/{head.json,queue.json,index-NNNN.jsonl}; events/{track}/{event_id}.json; media/{sha[:2]}/{sha}.mp4. Index lines are '<canonical_json>\t<ed25519_signature_hex>', append-only.

baselines._comment: The genesis king: BRL1's epoch0000 checkpoint (10.0% on its 200 held-out level-1 scenarios), converted to model.safetensors and published as robotensor/vector-base; weights_sha256 e0d6264795601d06b3f8ca48dde9e167b76ce84ae790d9e9148de030c60ae4d1.
